_: The countryside round the towns (countryside.gd; docs/TUNING.md). near_town: tiles kept clear round a town for its own fields. crop.sway: how far the ears move in a fresh breeze (about a fifth of their height at 1.2; the h-squared law in the shader); crop.cut: how low a reaped field's stubble stands; crop.reach: crops are drawn this near the camera (world units), the field's painted colour beyond. tuft_reach: grass tufts are drawn this near the camera.
_field_mix: countryside.gd FIELD_MIX: how much a ploughed field's painted crop covers the soil under it (was 0.55; g37: the far fields still hard bright blocks; field_ground_tints greyer too, gold 0.74, 0.66, 0.54).

field_ground_tints._: countryside.gd _ground_season: a strip's painted crop tinted by the stage its crop stands at (green, yellowing, gold, stubble; bare in winter), so the fields turn with the year past the crops' reach.

field_ground._: Each kind of field's painted ground (countryside.gd field_ground, the one place: the farmsteads' fields, the towns' worked strips in land_use.gd, the fallow behind a town): wheat and barley on the painted dry grass, cabbage, bean and flax strips on the painted grass, fallow on the ploughed field soil: each the ground layer's own calmed paint (tools/pack_painted_ground.gd <layer>-paint.png; g34: the raw painted_v2 paintings read as hard bright blocks from afar). Group render g1, the breach: the old striped wheat photo (field-wheat.jpg, orange 0.64, 0.46, 0.20) tiled from afar read as orange corduroy beside green strips.

tints._: countryside.gd TINTS: the standing grain's colour by stage, over its painted cards (muted, g33: bright lime and gold blocks; g35 siege: still yellow-green, green 0.46, 0.6, 0.38, was 0.5, 0.72, 0.36; g37 siege: still lime, the cards' own paint is yellow, so cooler: green 0.4, 0.52, 0.42, yellowing 0.66, 0.62, 0.5). rows_tint: cabbage and beans, a multiply on their scanned colours.

flax_tints._: countryside.gd FLAX_TINTS: flax by stage (was in code, gold at 1.25: a bright block; g35 siege).
